16.3.4.1.en: Xiao Li: Refusing doesn't actually mean you are unwilling to help.

16.3.4.2.text: 遇到解决不了的问题或者无法完成的任务时，拒绝正好说明你对朋友负责。
16.3.4.2.en: When you face a problem you cannot solve or a task you cannot complete, saying no shows that you take your responsibility to your friend seriously.

16.3.4.3.text: 这也是对你父母负责的态度。
16.3.4.3.en: It also shows responsibility toward your parents.

16.3.5.1.text: 小林：既然别人找我帮忙，说明他真的很需要我的帮助。
16.3.5.1.en: Xiao Lin: If someone asks me for help, it means he really needs it.

16.3.5.2.text: 我担心要是说“不”的话，会让他误会和伤心。
16.3.5.2.en: I'm worried that saying no will lead to a misunderstanding and hurt his feelings.

16.3.6.2.text: 如果你用一个既合适又礼貌的方法告诉朋友，他一定会原谅你的。
16.3.6.2.en: If you explain it to your friend in an appropriate and polite way, he will certainly understand and forgive you.

16.4.1.1.text: 有些同学经常把“明天”和“将来”挂在嘴边，常说作业明天再完成，下次考试一定好好儿复习，等等。
16.4.1.1.en: Some students are always talking about “tomorrow” and “the future,” saying that they will finish homework tomorrow or definitely revise properly for the next exam, and so on.

16.4.1.2.text: 这种态度会浪费时间，不但会让你到最后什么事情都做不成，而且还得不到别人的同情。
16.4.1.2.en: This attitude wastes time: you may end up achieving nothing and receive no sympathy from others either.

16.4.1.3.text: 所以不要把什么事情都推到“明天”，一切从现在做起。
16.4.1.3.en: So do not put everything off until “tomorrow.” Start now.

16.4.1.4.text: 就拿学汉语来说吧，首先要注意课前预习，找出第二天要学习的重点；其次，上课时要认真听，不能马虎；最后，课后要记得复习。
16.4.1.4.en: Take learning Chinese as an example. First, prepare before class and identify the key points for the next day's lesson; second, listen attentively in class and don't be careless; finally, remember to review afterward.

16.4.1.5.text: 只要这样，汉语就能越学越好，越说越自信。
16.4.1.5.en: Do this, and your Chinese will keep improving while you become more confident speaking it.

16.5.1.1.text: 当你认为自己在哪方面很优秀时，千万要冷静，不要骄傲。
16.5.1.1.en: When you think you are particularly good at something, stay level-headed and do not become arrogant.

16.5.1.2.text: 因为这个世界很大，“天外有天，人外有人”，很可能有人在这方面比你更厉害。
16.5.1.2.en: The world is vast, and “there is always someone better.” Someone else may well be more capable than you in that area.

16.5.1.3.text: 你现在是第一，并不表示你永远都是第一。
16.5.1.3.en: Being number one now does not mean you will always be number one.

16.5.1.4.text: 就像比赛一样，没有人会永远输，也没有人会一直赢。
16.5.1.4.en: As in a competition, nobody loses forever and nobody wins all the time.

16.5.1.5.text: 我们知道的越多，就会发现自己不懂的也越多。
16.5.1.5.en: The more we know, the more we discover that we do not understand.

16.5.1.6.text: 我们应该重视平时的积累，多向周围的人学习。
16.5.1.6.en: We should value steady learning and learn more from the people around us.

16.5.1.7.text: 如果你敢诚实地说出自己对哪方面不了解，并不说明自己比别人差，相反，这样做更能得到别人的尊重。
16.5.1.7.en: Having the courage to admit honestly that you do not understand something does not make you inferior. On the contrary, it earns other people's respect.

17.1.1.1.text: 小夏：最近天气越来越凉快了，风一刮，草地上就会有一层厚厚的黄叶，看来秋天已经到了。
17.1.1.1.en: Xiao Xia: The weather has been getting cooler. Whenever the wind blows, a thick layer of yellow leaves falls onto the grass. It looks as though autumn has arrived.

17.1.2.1.text: 安娜：这几天香山特别热闹，随着气温的降低，那里许多植物的叶子都由绿变黄或者变红，吸引了很多游客参观，咱们今天也去看看吧。
17.1.2.1.en: Anna: The Fragrant Hills have been especially lively lately. As temperatures fall, many plants' leaves turn from green to yellow or red, attracting lots of visitors. Let's go and have a look today too.

17.1.3.1.text: 小夏：你看天上的云，今天肯定有大雨。
17.1.3.1.en: Xiao Xia: Look at those clouds. It is definitely going to rain heavily today.

17.1.3.2.text: 再说，香山上看红叶的人太多了。
17.1.3.2.en: Besides, there are too many people looking at the autumn leaves in the Fragrant Hills.

17.1.3.3.text: 咱们改天去长城吧，广播里说那里也有不少专门看红叶的好地方。
17.1.3.3.en: Let's go to the Great Wall another day. The radio said there are plenty of good spots for viewing red leaves there too.

17.1.4.1.text: 安娜：真可惜，我还想多照点儿香山的照片呢。
17.1.4.1.en: Anna: What a pity. I wanted to take more photos of the Fragrant Hills.

17.1.4.2.text: 去长城倒是一个好主意，那我们明天去吧。
17.1.4.2.en: Going to the Great Wall is a good idea, though. Let's go tomorrow.

17.1.5.1.text: 小夏：明天恐怕也不行，明天是我爸的生日。
17.1.5.1.en: Xiao Xia: I'm afraid tomorrow won't work either. It is my dad's birthday.

17.1.6.1.text: 安娜：没关系，那我们再约时间。
17.1.6.1.en: Anna: No problem. We can arrange another time.

17.2.1.1.text: 小林：你的这只大黑狗毛真漂亮，而且这么聪明，每次见了都想抱一抱它。
17.2.1.1.en: Xiao Lin: Your big black dog has such beautiful fur and is so clever. Every time I see it, I want to give it a hug.

17.2.2.1.text: 小李：狗是很聪明的动物，只要稍微花点儿时间教教它，它就能学会很多东西。
17.2.2.1.en: Xiao Li: Dogs are very intelligent animals. Spend a little time teaching them, and they can learn lots of things.

17.2.3.1.text: 小林：听你这么一说，我现在也想养一只狗了。
17.2.3.1.en: Xiao Lin: Hearing you say that makes me want to get a dog too.

17.2.3.2.text: 每次你让它干什么，它就像能听懂你的话一样去做。
17.2.3.2.en: Whenever you ask it to do something, it does it as if it understands your words.

17.2.3.3.text: 你教它是不是用了什么特别的方法？
17.2.3.3.en: Did you use some special method to train it?

17.2.4.1.text: 小李：要让它完成一些任务，只教一次是不够的，应该耐心地一遍一遍地教给它，使它熟悉，然后它就会严格按照你的要求做了。
17.2.4.1.en: Xiao Li: To teach it a task, showing it once isn't enough. You have to teach it patiently over and over until it is familiar with the task; then it will do exactly as you ask.

17.2.5.1.text: 小林：看来没有想的那么容易。
17.2.5.1.en: Xiao Lin: It sounds less easy than I imagined.

17.2.6.1.text: 小李：狗是我们的好朋友，它能听懂人的话，明白人的心情。
17.2.6.1.en: Xiao Li: Dogs are our good friends. They can understand what we say and sense our moods.

17.2.6.2.text: 在你心里难受的时候，它会一直陪着你。
17.2.6.2.en: When you feel upset, they will stay by your side.

17.3.1.1.text: 马克：上个月我去了趟北京动物园，那里约有500种动物，听导游说北京动物园是亚洲最大的动物园之一。
17.3.1.1.en: Mark: Last month I visited Beijing Zoo, which has about five hundred animal species. The guide said it is one of Asia's largest zoos.

17.3.2.1.text: 小夏：去年放暑假的时候，我也去过一次，我在那儿看了马、熊猫、老虎等动物。
17.3.2.1.en: Xiao Xia: I went there once during last year's summer vacation too. I saw horses, pandas, tigers, and other animals.

17.3.2.2.text: 我特别喜欢熊猫，可惜它们当时大多在睡觉。
17.3.2.2.en: I especially like pandas, but unfortunately most of them were sleeping at the time.

17.3.3.1.text: 马克：我去的那天正赶上六一儿童节，许多父母带着孩子去动物园。
17.3.3.1.en: Mark: My visit happened to fall on Children's Day, June 1, and many parents brought their children to the zoo.

17.3.3.2.text: 入口处排队的人很多，动物园里热闹极了。
17.3.3.2.en: There was a long queue at the entrance, and the zoo was bustling.

17.3.3.3.text: 熊猫们也变得特别活泼，我还给它们照了不少照片呢。
17.3.3.3.en: The pandas were particularly lively too, and I took quite a few photos of them.

17.3.4.1.text: 小夏：大熊猫身子胖胖的，样子可爱极了。
17.3.4.1.en: Xiao Xia: Giant pandas have such chubby bodies and look incredibly cute.

17.3.5.1.text: 马克：不过，它们数量不多，现在全世界一共才有一千多只吧。
17.3.5.1.en: Mark: There aren't many of them, though. There are only a little over a thousand in the whole world, aren't there?

17.3.6.1.text: 小夏：以前只有中国有大熊猫，为了表示友好，从1957年开始，中国把大熊猫作为礼物送给其他一些国家。
17.3.6.1.en: Xiao Xia: Giant pandas used to be found only in China. Starting in 1957, China gave pandas to some other countries as a gesture of friendship.

17.3.6.2.text: 现在，很多国家的人们在本国都能看到大熊猫了。
17.3.6.2.en: Now people in many countries can see giant pandas in their own country.

17.4.1.1.text: 不仅社会上的人与人之间有竞争，森林里的各种植物之间也有竞争，这一点儿也不奇怪。
17.4.1.1.en: Competition exists not only among people in society but also among the various plants in forests, which is not at all surprising.

17.4.1.2.text: 植物会为了阳光、空气和水而竞争。
17.4.1.2.en: Plants compete for sunlight, air, and water.

17.4.1.3.text: 一些高大的植物往往能获得更多的阳光、空气和水，而剩下的一些比较低矮的植物就只能长在这些高大植物的下面。
17.4.1.3.en: Tall plants often obtain more sunlight, air, and water, while the shorter plants left over can only grow beneath them.

17.4.1.4.text: 由于气候条件不同，世界各地植物叶子的样子也很不相同。
17.4.1.4.en: Because climatic conditions vary, plant leaves look very different in different parts of the world.

17.4.1.5.text: 在暖和、水分比较多的地方，叶子往往长得又大又厚；在阳光特别厉害、水分少的地方，叶子就会长得又细又长。
17.4.1.5.en: In warm places with plenty of moisture, leaves often grow large and thick; in places with intense sunshine and little water, they grow thin and long.

17.5.1.1.text: 地球上大约71%的地方是蓝色的海洋，在美丽的海底世界里，生活着各种各样的植物和动物。
17.5.1.1.en: Blue oceans cover about 71% of the Earth, and their beautiful underwater world is home to all kinds of plants and animals.

17.5.1.2.text: 我们小时候都听过美人鱼的故事，其实真正的海底世界比故事里写的更美。
17.5.1.2.en: We all heard mermaid stories as children, but the real underwater world is even more beautiful than the stories describe.

17.5.1.3.text: 科学研究发现，海洋底部看上去非常安静，然而却不是一点儿声音也没有，海底的动物们一直在“说话”，只不过人的耳朵是听不到的。
17.5.1.3.en: Research has found that although the ocean floor appears very quiet, it is not completely silent. Underwater animals are constantly “talking,” but human ears cannot hear them.

17.5.1.4.text: 另外，就算在几公里深的海底也仍然能看到东西，许多鱼会发出各种颜色的亮光，像一个个排列起来的灯，美极了，就像在梦里一样。
17.5.1.4.en: Even several kilometers below the surface, it is still possible to see things: many fish give off lights of different colors, like rows of lamps. It is breathtaking, almost like a dream.

18.1.1.1.text: 孙月：上次女儿问我飞机是怎么起飞和降落的，真不知道该怎么回答她，她现在总是有各种各样的“为什么”。
18.1.1.1.en: Sun Yue: The other day, my daughter asked me how airplanes take off and land, and I really didn't know how to answer. These days she is always asking “why” about everything.

18.1.2.1.text: 王静：孩子眼中的世界是美丽和奇特的。
18.1.2.1.en: Wang Jing: To children, the world is beautiful and full of wonders.

18.1.2.2.text: 有一本书叫《新十万个为什么》，现在卖得非常火。
18.1.2.2.en: There is a book called The New Hundred Thousand Whys that is selling extremely well now.

18.1.2.3.text: 书里的内容都是儿童想知道的科学知识，相信你女儿一定喜欢读。
18.1.2.3.en: It covers scientific facts that children want to know. I'm sure your daughter would enjoy reading it.

18.1.3.1.text: 孙月：难道它和我们小时候看的《十万个为什么》不一样吗？
18.1.3.1.en: Sun Yue: Is it different from the Hundred Thousand Whys we read as children?

18.1.4.1.text: 王静：作者的名字我没记住。
18.1.4.1.en: Wang Jing: I can't remember the author's name.

18.1.4.2.text: 《新十万个为什么》的内容更新，介绍了各种科学知识，包括地球、动物、植物、交通、科学技术、社会和文化等很多方面。
18.1.4.2.en: The new book is more up to date and introduces scientific knowledge in many areas, including the Earth, animals, plants, transport, science and technology, society, and culture.

18.1.5.2.text: 不过她这么小，我不知道她是否能读懂。
18.1.5.2.en: But she's so young that I'm not sure whether she will understand it.

18.1.6.1.text: 王静：放心吧，这本书的语言简单易懂，一定能增长孩子的科学知识。
18.1.6.1.en: Wang Jing: Don't worry. The language is simple and easy to understand, so it is sure to expand her scientific knowledge.

18.2.1.1.text: 李老师：现在的大学生一遇到不明白的问题，可以马上在网上查找答案，几秒钟就把问题解决了，这比我们上学的时候方便多了。
18.2.1.1.en: Teacher Li: Nowadays, when university students encounter something they don't understand, they can search online and solve the problem in seconds. It is much more convenient than when we were students.

18.2.2.1.text: 高老师：现在的人们，尤其是大学生开始普遍使用电脑，他们的生活已经离不开电脑。
18.2.2.1.en: Teacher Gao: Computers are now widely used, especially among university students, whose lives have become inseparable from them.

18.2.2.2.text: 据调查，70%的人遇到问题时，首先想到的就是上网找答案。
18.2.2.2.en: According to a survey, 70% of people first think of looking online for an answer when they encounter a problem.

18.2.3.1.text: 李老师：电脑和互联网技术的发展使学生们的学习方式发生了很多变化，不过天天对着电脑看，眼睛实在受不了。
18.2.3.1.en: Teacher Li: Developments in computers and the internet have greatly changed how students learn, but looking at a computer every day is really hard on the eyes.

18.2.4.1.text: 高老师：不仅是学习方式，而且连生活方式也发生了很大改变。
18.2.4.1.en: Teacher Gao: Not just the way people study—even the way they live has changed a great deal.

18.2.4.2.text: 现在越来越多的学生喜欢在网上写日记，他们说这样可以让朋友及时了解自己的生活。
18.2.4.2.en: More and more students enjoy keeping online diaries, saying that these let friends keep up with their lives.

18.2.5.1.text: 李老师：这个办法不错，既能方便大家的交流，还能节约用纸，保护环境。
18.2.5.1.en: Teacher Li: That's a good idea. It makes communication easier, saves paper, and protects the environment.

18.2.5.2.text: 但是如果别人都能看到我的日记的话，多不安全啊！
18.2.5.2.en: But if everyone could read my diary, that wouldn't be very secure!

18.2.6.1.text: 高老师：放心吧，可以给网上的日记加密码，那样只有得到了允许，别人才能看到。
18.2.6.1.en: Teacher Gao: Don't worry. You can password-protect an online diary so that others can only view it with permission.

18.3.1.1.text: 王静：我昨天晚上做了一个特别奇怪的梦，梦到自己正在一座桥上走，走着走着，突然开过来一辆车，非常危险，接着又梦见我跳到车上，跟警察一起抓住了一个坏人。
18.3.1.1.en: Wang Jing: I had a very strange dream last night. I was walking across a bridge when a car suddenly came toward me—it was dangerous. Then I dreamed that I jumped onto the car and helped the police catch a criminal.

18.3.2.1.text: 孙月：奇怪，你怎么总能记住自己做了什么梦？
18.3.2.1.en: Sun Yue: That's strange. How can you always remember what you dreamed?

18.3.2.2.en: I don't think I have ever dreamed at all.

18.3.3.1.text: 王静：每个人都会做梦，区别只是有多有少。
18.3.3.1.en: Wang Jing: Everyone dreams; people just differ in how much they dream.

18.3.3.2.text: 有的人睡醒之后还记得梦里的事情，有的人却记不清楚了。
18.3.3.2.en: Some people remember what happened in their dreams after waking, while others cannot remember clearly.

18.3.3.3.text: 你之所以觉得从来没做过梦，只不过是忘记了。
18.3.3.3.en: You only think you have never dreamed because you have forgotten your dreams.

18.3.4.1.text: 孙月：你说的有道理，我一般都是一觉睡到天亮。
18.3.4.1.en: Sun Yue: That makes sense. I usually sleep straight through until morning.

18.3.4.2.text: 很多人认为做梦是上天要告诉他们将来会发生的一些事情，可能上天不想让我知道吧。
18.3.4.2.en: Many people think dreams are heaven's way of telling them what will happen in the future. Perhaps heaven doesn't want me to know!

18.3.5.1.text: 王静：一般晚上睡觉时，身体感觉到什么，人就容易梦到什么内容。
18.3.5.1.en: Wang Jing: What your body senses while you sleep often influences what you dream about.

18.3.5.2.text: 记得有一次，我晚饭吃得太咸，那天晚上就梦见自己到处找商店买矿泉水。
18.3.5.2.en: I remember once eating a very salty dinner and then dreaming that I was searching everywhere for a shop selling mineral water.

18.3.6.1.text: 孙月：很多人都试着对梦进行解释，有些人甚至专门写过这方面的书，可惜到现在仍然没有一个科学的说法。
18.3.6.1.en: Sun Yue: Many people have tried interpreting dreams, and some have even written books specifically about them. Unfortunately, there is still no scientific explanation.

18.4.1.1.text: 现在手机不但价格降低了，而且作用也越来越大，打电话、发短信已经成了人们普遍使用的联系方法。
18.4.1.1.en: Mobile phones have not only become cheaper but also increasingly useful, and calling and texting have become common ways to stay in touch.

18.4.1.2.text: 除此以外，你还可以用它来听音乐、看电影、阅读、玩儿游戏、付款购物等，这大大方便了人们的生活。
18.4.1.2.en: Besides that, phones let you listen to music, watch films, read, play games, and pay for shopping, making everyday life much more convenient.

18.4.1.3.text: 举一个例子，迷路时，只要用手机地图查一下地址，马上就能知道怎么去那个地点。
18.4.1.3.en: For example, if you get lost, simply look up the address on your phone's map and you can immediately find out how to get there.

18.4.1.4.text: 现在的手机更像是一部可以拿在手中的电脑，现代人的生活已经越来越离不开手机了。
18.4.1.4.en: Today's mobile phone is more like a handheld computer, and modern life is becoming increasingly inseparable from it.

18.5.1.1.text: 21世纪，我们的生活发生了巨大变化。
18.5.1.1.en: Our lives have changed enormously in the twenty-first century.

18.5.1.2.text: 几千公里以外的国家，以前坐船需要几个月，现在乘坐飞机不过十几个小时。
18.5.1.2.en: Reaching a country thousands of kilometers away once took months by sea; now it takes only a dozen or so hours by plane.

18.5.1.3.text: 原来寄信需要好几天，现在连邮局都不用去，只要在家里上网发个电子邮件，用不了一分钟，远处的朋友就能收到，比写信封用的时间都短。
18.5.1.3.en: A letter used to take days to arrive. Now, without even visiting the post office, you can send an email from home and a distant friend will receive it in less than a minute—less time than addressing an envelope.

18.5.1.4.text: 以前外地的新闻要几天后才能知道，现在只要打开网站，任何信息都可以在第一时间获得。
18.5.1.4.en: News from elsewhere once took days to reach us, but now opening a website gives us immediate access to information.

18.5.1.5.text: 现代科学技术的发展让世界变得越来越小，所以现在人们都把地球叫作“地球村”。
18.5.1.5.en: Modern science and technology have made the world feel smaller and smaller, which is why people now call it a “global village.”

19.1.1.2.text: 我希望下个学期在这里继续学习，请问还需要重新申请吗？
19.1.1.2.en: I would like to continue studying here next semester. Do I need to apply again?

19.1.2.2.text: 给你表格，出生年月、性别、护照号码都要填，还有联系地址、联系电话。
19.1.2.2.en: Here is the form. Fill in your date of birth, gender, passport number, contact address, and telephone number.

19.1.3.1.text: 马克：真抱歉，我不小心把护照号码填错了，您能再给我一份新的申请表吗？
19.1.3.1.en: Mark: I'm very sorry, but I accidentally entered my passport number incorrectly. Could you give me another application form?

19.1.4.1.text: 高老师：没关系，不用道歉，谁都有粗心填错的时候。
19.1.4.1.en: Teacher Gao: That's all right. There is no need to apologize; everyone makes careless mistakes sometimes.

19.1.4.2.text: 申请表都被别人拿走了，我给你重新打印一份，你等一下。
19.1.4.2.en: The other forms have all been taken, so I'll print a new one for you. Please wait a moment.

19.1.5.1.en: (Teacher Gao prints the form, and Mark fills it in.)

19.1.6.1.text: 马克：这次我按照要求都填写完了，请问还需要做别的事情吗？
19.1.6.1.en: Mark: This time I have completed everything as required. Is there anything else I need to do?

19.1.7.1.text: 高老师：请把你的护照给我，我们要把护照复印一下。
19.1.7.1.en: Teacher Gao: Please give me your passport. We need to make a photocopy.

19.2.1.1.text: 李进：呀，你的手怎么流血了？
19.2.1.1.en: Li Jin: Oh! Why is your hand bleeding?

19.2.1.2.en: Wait a moment. I'll bandage it for you.

19.2.2.1.text: 王静：没关系，我想给你做点儿羊肉饺子，刚才用刀切肉的时候把手弄破了。
19.2.2.1.en: Wang Jing: It's all right. I wanted to make you some lamb dumplings and cut my hand while chopping the meat just now.

19.2.3.1.text: 李进：你也太不小心了，不过好像不太严重，过几天就好了。
19.2.3.1.en: Li Jin: You were really careless, but it doesn't look too serious. It should heal in a few days.

19.2.3.2.text: 衣服上也有一点儿血，你把衣服脱下来，我给你洗洗。
19.2.3.2.en: There's a little blood on your clothes too. Take them off and I'll wash them for you.

19.2.4.1.text: 王静：看来今天吃不上羊肉饺子了。
19.2.4.1.en: Wang Jing: It looks as though we won't be having lamb dumplings today.

19.2.5.1.text: 李进：那我们就吃点儿别的。
19.2.5.1.en: Li Jin: Then let's eat something else.

19.2.5.2.text: 我常去的那家理发店附近有个餐厅，那里的包子很好吃，我一会儿去买一点儿。
19.2.5.2.en: There is a restaurant near the barbershop I often visit, and its steamed buns are delicious. I'll go and buy some in a little while.

19.2.6.1.text: 王静：好吧，我衣服口袋里有十几块零钱，买包子应该够。
19.2.6.1.en: Wang Jing: All right. There are ten-odd yuan in change in my pocket, which should be enough for the buns.

19.3.1.1.text: 马克：我早上跟你打招呼，你没看见。
19.3.1.1.en: Mark: I said hello to you this morning, but you didn't see me.

19.3.1.2.text: 想不到又在这儿碰见你了。
19.3.1.2.en: I didn't expect to run into you here again.

19.3.2.1.text: 安娜：真是对不起，我不是故意的，今天早上我忘戴眼镜了，看不清楚。
19.3.2.1.en: Anna: I'm really sorry. It wasn't deliberate. I forgot to wear my glasses this morning and couldn't see clearly.

19.3.3.1.text: 马克：刚才我在旁边看到你跳中国舞了，没看出来你跳得这么好！
19.3.3.1.en: Mark: I saw you doing a Chinese dance over there just now. I had no idea you danced so well!

19.3.3.2.text: 难道你以前在你们国家就学过中国舞蹈吗？
19.3.3.2.en: Had you already studied Chinese dance in your own country?

19.3.4.1.text: 安娜：我小时候妈妈教我跳过两年的舞，所以稍微有点儿基础。
19.3.4.1.en: Anna: My mother taught me to dance for two years when I was little, so I have a bit of a foundation.

19.3.4.2.text: 再说，舞蹈不仅是一门艺术，也是一种“语言”，这种语言与国籍无关，无论哪个国家的人都能看懂。
19.3.4.2.en: Besides, dance is not just an art but also a “language.” It has nothing to do with nationality; people from any country can understand it.

19.3.5.2.text: 我刚学习跳这种舞没多久，你帮我看看，我的这个动作对不对。
19.3.5.2.en: I have only recently started learning this dance. Could you check whether I'm doing this movement correctly?

19.3.6.1.text: 安娜：你这个动作做得还是不太标准，我给你跳一遍。
19.3.6.1.en: Anna: Your movement still isn't quite right. I'll demonstrate it for you.

19.3.6.2.text: 你仔细看着，应该像我这样：先抬胳膊，然后抬腿，最后头再向右转一下。
19.3.6.2.en: Watch carefully. Do it like this: first raise your arms, then lift your leg, and finally turn your head slightly to the right.

19.4.1.1.text: 马克去年租的房子离马路很近，对面有大大小小的商店，周围环境非常吵。
19.4.1.1.en: The flat Mark rented last year was near a main road, with shops of all sizes opposite, so the neighborhood was very noisy.

19.4.1.2.text: 所以，房子还没到期，马克就开始着急换房子了。
19.4.1.2.en: He therefore became eager to move even before the lease expired.

19.4.1.3.text: 有一天，他在小区门口看到一个租房子的广告。
19.4.1.3.en: One day, he saw a rental advertisement at the entrance to the residential complex.

19.4.1.4.text: 广告上说房子交通方便，周围很安静，厨房很大。
19.4.1.4.en: It described a flat with convenient transport, quiet surroundings, and a large kitchen.

19.4.1.5.text: 总的来说，这套房子他很满意，于是他就记下了房东的手机号码。
19.4.1.5.en: Overall, he was very pleased with it, so he wrote down the landlord's mobile number.

19.4.1.6.text: 可回家后打电话，电话总是占线。
19.4.1.6.en: But when he called after getting home, the line was always busy.

19.4.1.7.text: 第二天，他路过小区门口时，又仔细看了一下广告，原来在记号码的时候写错了一个数字。
19.4.1.7.en: The next day, he passed the entrance again and checked the advertisement carefully. He realized he had copied one digit of the number incorrectly.

19.5.1.1.text: 很多外国人认为所有中国人都会功夫和乒乓球，其实只是喜爱这两种运动的中国人比较多。
19.5.1.1.en: Many foreigners think all Chinese people know kung fu and can play table tennis, but in fact these are simply two sports that many Chinese people enjoy.

19.5.1.2.text: 中国人特别喜欢打乒乓球，在中国你会发现到处都有乒乓球桌。
19.5.1.2.en: Chinese people particularly enjoy table tennis, and you can find table tennis tables everywhere in China.

19.5.1.3.text: 像乒乓球、羽毛球、跑步等运动对条件要求不高，所以它们都成为人们运动不错的选择。
19.5.1.3.en: Sports such as table tennis, badminton, and running do not require elaborate facilities or conditions, making them good exercise choices.

19.5.1.4.text: 人们常说“生命在于运动”，所以很多人一到周末就会到体育馆打几场球。
19.5.1.4.en: People often say, “Life lies in movement,” so many go to sports centers on weekends to play a few games.

19.5.1.5.text: “乒乓球”这个名字也很有意思，“乒”和“乓”就是打球时发出的声音。
19.5.1.5.en: The Chinese name for table tennis, “ping-pong,” is interesting too: “ping” and “pong” imitate the sounds of the ball being hit.

19.5.1.6.text: 在看乒乓球比赛时，尤其是在运动员发球的时候，观众要安静，禁止大声讲话或者离开座位随便走动。
19.5.1.6.en: Spectators at table tennis matches must remain quiet, especially during a serve. Loud conversation and leaving one's seat to wander around are prohibited.

20.1.1.1.text: 朋友：该加油了，去机场的路上有加油站吗？
20.1.1.1.en: Friend: We need petrol. Is there a filling station on the way to the airport?

20.1.2.1.text: 小张：我记得过了长江大桥往右一拐就有一个，大概有四五公里远。
20.1.2.1.en: Xiao Zhang: I remember one just after you cross the Yangtze River Bridge and turn right. It's about four or five kilometers away.

20.1.3.1.text: 朋友：好，那我就放心了，别开着开着没油了。
20.1.3.1.en: Friend: Good, that's a relief. We don't want to run out of fuel while driving.

20.1.3.2.text: 你去北京的航班是几点的？
20.1.3.2.en: What time is your flight to Beijing?

20.1.3.3.en: Will we make it in time?

20.1.4.1.text: 小张：航班本来是十点的，后来机场网站上通知推迟了一个小时，所以九点半以前到就应该没问题。
20.1.4.1.en: Xiao Zhang: The flight was originally at ten, but the airport website later announced a one-hour delay, so arriving before half past nine should be fine.

20.1.5.1.text: 朋友：刚才我还有点儿担心来不及呢。
20.1.5.1.en: Friend: I was a little worried just now that we wouldn't make it.

20.1.5.2.text: 一会儿加完油，往西走五百米就能上高速公路。
20.1.5.2.en: After we fill up, we can drive five hundred meters west to join the expressway.

20.1.5.3.text: 走高速公路大约半个小时就到了。
20.1.5.3.en: From there, it is about half an hour to the airport.

20.1.6.1.text: 小张：一会儿我自己进去换登机牌，你就不用送我了，等我到了首都机场再给你发短信。
20.1.6.1.en: Xiao Zhang: I'll go in and collect my boarding pass myself, so you don't need to come with me. I'll text you when I arrive at Beijing Capital Airport.

20.2.1.1.text: 孙月：女儿下个星期就要放寒假了，到时候咱们带她去旅游，放松放松，怎么样？
20.2.1.1.en: Sun Yue: Our daughter's winter vacation starts next week. How about taking her on a trip so we can all relax?

20.2.2.1.text: 丈夫：平时女儿那么多课，总是说想去旅行，但是没时间，怪可怜的。
20.2.2.1.en: Husband: She usually has so many classes and is always saying she wants to travel but has no time. I feel sorry for her.

20.2.2.2.text: 这次放假咱们带她去哪儿玩儿比较好呢？
20.2.2.2.en: Where would be a good place to take her during this holiday?

20.2.3.1.text: 孙月：去年我同事带她儿子去广西玩儿了一趟，听说很不错，我们就去广西吧。
20.2.3.1.en: Sun Yue: A colleague took her son to Guangxi last year and said it was very nice. Let's go there.

20.2.4.1.text: 丈夫：好啊，那里的气候和北方很不同，即使是冬天，也非常暖和，还能吃到许多新鲜的水果。
20.2.4.1.en: Husband: Good idea. The climate there is very different from the north: even in winter, it is warm, and we can enjoy lots of fresh fruit.

20.2.4.2.text: 等女儿一回来我就告诉她这个好消息。
20.2.4.2.en: I'll tell our daughter the good news as soon as she gets home.

20.2.5.1.en: Sun Yue: Don't tell her just yet.

20.2.5.2.text: 中午我们不是要去对面的饭店吃烤鸭，祝贺她考试成绩都合格吗？
20.2.5.2.en: Aren't we going to the restaurant opposite for roast duck at lunchtime to celebrate her passing all her exams?

20.2.5.3.text: 那时候再告诉她，不是更好？
20.2.5.3.en: Wouldn't it be better to tell her then?

20.2.6.1.text: 丈夫：好主意，到时她知道了肯定特别开心。
20.2.6.1.en: Husband: Good idea. She will be delighted when she finds out.

20.3.1.1.text: 马克：这么多照片，都是你这次去丽江旅行时照的？
20.3.1.1.en: Mark: There are so many photos. Did you take all of them on your recent trip to Lijiang?

20.3.1.2.text: 那里的自然风景可真美！
20.3.1.2.en: The natural scenery there is beautiful!

20.3.2.1.text: 安娜：是啊，小城四季的风景都很美，而且环境保护得也很好，因此每年都吸引着成千上万的游客去那儿旅游。
20.3.2.1.en: Anna: Yes. The little town is beautiful in every season and its environment is well protected, so it attracts tens of thousands of visitors every year.

20.3.3.1.text: 马克：这张照片上和你干杯的那个人是少数民族吗？
20.3.3.1.en: Mark: Is the person raising a toast with you in this photo from an ethnic minority?

20.3.4.1.text: 安娜：她是我们的导游，不是少数民族。
20.3.4.1.en: Anna: She's our tour guide, and she isn't from an ethnic minority.

20.3.4.2.text: 一路上她给我们讲了很多有趣的笑话。
20.3.4.2.en: She told us lots of funny jokes along the way.

20.3.4.3.text: 有一次我把存包的钥匙丢了，最后还是她帮我找到的。
20.3.4.3.en: Once, I lost the key for my stored bag, and she was the one who helped me find it.

20.3.4.4.text: 这张照片就是找到钥匙后，我们一起照的。
20.3.4.4.en: We took this photo together after finding the key.

20.3.5.1.text: 马克：明年我有机会也去那儿看看，到时把你的导游介绍给我吧。
20.3.5.1.en: Mark: If I get the chance, I'll visit next year too. Please introduce me to your guide then.

20.3.5.2.text: 究竟哪个季节去丽江旅游比较好呢？
20.3.5.2.en: Which season is actually best for visiting Lijiang?

20.3.6.1.text: 安娜：那儿最美的季节是春天和秋天，不过那时候人比较多。
20.3.6.1.en: Anna: Spring and autumn are the most beautiful seasons there, but they are also more crowded.

20.3.6.2.text: 稍微好一点儿的时间是每年12月到第二年3月。
20.3.6.2.en: A somewhat better time to go is from December to March of the following year.

20.3.6.3.text: 这段时间去丽江的话，无论交通还是吃、住都很便宜。
20.3.6.3.en: During that period, transport, food, and accommodation in Lijiang are all very inexpensive.

20.4.1.1.text: 中国南北距离约5500公里，因此南北气候有很大区别。
20.4.1.1.en: China stretches about 5,500 kilometers from north to south, so the climates of the two regions differ greatly.

20.4.1.2.text: 每年三四月份的时候，如果从北方坐火车到南方去旅游，一路上你会发现，不同的地方有不同的风景：窗外的树一棵一棵地变绿，北方也许还下着雪，南方却已经到处都是绿色了。
20.4.1.2.en: If you travel south by train in March or April, you will see the scenery change along the way: the trees outside gradually turn green, and while it may still be snowing in the north, the south is already green everywhere.

20.4.1.3.text: 南方菜很有特点，特别是汤，味道鲜美，很多北方人都喜欢喝。
20.4.1.3.en: Southern cuisine has distinctive qualities, especially its delicious soups, which many northerners enjoy.

20.4.1.4.text: 另外，南方和北方的语言也有很大不同。
20.4.1.4.en: The languages spoken in northern and southern China also differ greatly.

20.4.1.5.text: 比如你跟上海人对话时，会发现上海话听起来就像外语一样。
20.4.1.5.en: For example, when you talk with people from Shanghai, Shanghainese can sound like a foreign language.

20.4.1.6.text: 虽然上海人也会讲普通话，可是仔细听，还是有上海味儿。
20.4.1.6.en: Although people from Shanghai also speak Mandarin, you can still hear a Shanghai accent if you listen closely.

20.5.1.1.text: 一个人有时间一定要去旅行，旅行不仅能丰富一个人的经历，而且是很好的减压方法。
20.5.1.1.en: Whenever you have time, you should travel. Traveling not only enriches your experience but is also an excellent way to reduce stress.

20.5.1.2.text: 但对我来说，最重要的是旅行能让我有机会尝到各地有名的小吃。
20.5.1.2.en: For me, though, the most important thing is the chance to try famous local snacks from different places.

20.5.1.3.text: 放假的时候，我会收拾好行李，带上地图，买张火车票，向目的地出发。
20.5.1.3.en: During holidays, I pack my luggage, take a map, buy a train ticket, and set off for my destination.

20.5.1.4.text: 说起吃的东西，给我印象最深的是湖南菜。
20.5.1.4.en: When it comes to food, Hunan cuisine has left the deepest impression on me.

20.5.1.5.text: 湖南菜的特点就是辣，与其他地方的辣不同，湖南菜的辣主要是咸辣、香辣和酸辣。
20.5.1.5.en: Hunan food is known for its spiciness, but its heat differs from that of other regions: it is mainly salty and spicy, fragrant and spicy, or sour and spicy.

20.5.1.6.text: 虽然全国各地都有湖南饭馆儿，但最好还是直接去那里尝一尝。
20.5.1.6.en: Although Hunan restaurants can be found all over China, it is best to go there and taste the food for yourself.

20.5.1.7.text: 每次旅行结束后，我都会精神百倍地开始我的工作。
20.5.1.7.en: After every trip, I return to work full of renewed energy.
